title: Fallbacks & Fallthroughs Cheatmap — Compact Field Guide (Draft)
body:
Purpose:
A compact, field-friendly reference for GTM and SEs to triage production inference degradations and present deterministic fallback options to customers. Focused on: rapid diagnosis, safe fallbacks, customer-facing language, and minimal ops friction.

Audience:
- Platform sellers, SEs, and on-call R&D engineers who need a short checklist to resolve or communicate degradations during demos, pilots, and escalation calls.

TL;DR (two lines):
If an inference request fails or SLOs break, classify: latency / cost / quality / capacity / region. Pick the least-invasive fallback path (routing variant -> quantized model -> reduced seq length -> cached-response) and communicate the tradeoff using the one-liner below.

One-liner fallback script (copy-paste for calls):
"We have a safe fallback path that preserves correctness while reducing latency and cost — we route to a compact variant (or cached prefix) for live traffic and run a background replay to validate outputs against the primary model; we'll roll the main back once throughput normalizes."

Quick decision flow (4 steps):
1) Detect & classify (trigger: latency > SLO x2 for 2 minutes OR token cost jump >30% week-over-week).
2) Scope impact (percentage of users/routes affected, model id, region).
3) Apply least-invasive fallback (see fallback ladder below).
4) Observe for 5–15 minutes; if stable, keep in degraded mode and notify stakeholders; if not, escalate to dedicated capacity or region failover.

Fallback ladder (ordered by least to most invasive):
- Route to warm KV-cached responses for repeated prompts (no model change).
- Route to a quantized-compatible model variant (same weights, lower precision).
- Route to a smaller architecture family variant (e.g., 13B -> 7B tuned for this workload).
- Reduce max_tokens / force early-stop heuristics for non-critical routes.
- Thin-out context (trim system+user history) for chat-heavy sessions.
- Move traffic to Dedicated pool or alternate region (if available).

Scenario cards (short versions for quick lookup):
1) Latency spike in hosted region (symptoms: p95 > 2x baseline; errors rare)
- Immediate action: enable routing policy to fall back to quantized variant for the affected region.
- Recommended variant: model-x-small-q8 (tested for parity on intent tasks).
- Sales talking points: "We can preserve intent accuracy while cutting response time and cost."
- Demo snippet (API): {endpoint: /v1/generate, model: model-x-small-q8, priority: high}
- Rollback criteria: p95 <= baseline *1.15 for 30 minutes.

2) Dedicated capacity saturation during pilot (symptoms: queuing, increased 429s)
- Immediate action: shift non-critical routes to shared-hosted fallback; notify CS and propose reserve burst.
- Recommended variant: Shared hosted model with prefix cache enabled.
- Sales talking points: "We can keep mission-critical flows working while we provision an additional pool."
- Rollback: provisioned nodes online + queue cleared for 15 minutes.

3) Model output regression after rollout (symptoms: increased QA-derived false positives or eval set drop)
- Immediate action: initiate automatic rollback to prior version; enable canary routing with 0% -> 10% -> 50% ramp once fixes land.
- Sales talking points: "We run canary validations and can revert instantly to preserve product quality."
- Linked artifacts: JIRA ticket to triage and Confluence eval logs.

4) Cost runaway detected (symptoms: token spend +40% M/M without usage growth)
- Immediate action: apply token_budget cap on high-cost routes and switch to compact model variants for conversational assistants.
- Sales talking points: "We can cap runaway spend per route and switch to cost-optimized models with marginal UX tradeoffs."

5) Region or cloud provider outage (symptoms: entire region 5xx)
- Immediate action: enable cross-region routing; use region-fallback policy to nearest available.
- Customer-facing phrasing: "Traffic will be routed to the next-best region — latency may change but availability is preserved."

6) Private deployment handshake or KMS failure (symptoms: auth failures or blocked keys)
- Immediate action: fall back to hosted sandbox with redaction and no-PII mode; open support case with private deploy team.
- Sales talking points: "For regulated pilots we have a sandbox continuity path while keys are restored."

Short objection response snippets (for SEs):
- "Why not just scale GPUs?" -> "Scaling is an option, but it takes time and increases unit cost; our fallbacks keep customer flows live while we provision capacity or optimize model selection."
- "Won't fallbacks break quality?" -> "We choose variants validated on your prompt set and run parallel replay to measure regressions before fully switching."
- "How do we guarantee no data leak when moving regions?" -> "We follow customer-configured data residency rules; region failover respects routing policy and data governance settings."

Demo playbook (2-minute script for SEs):
- Setup: Prior to demo, enable a canary route for a demo model and have a compact fallback ready.
- Mid-demo: Trigger a simulated latency spike (use internal chaos toggle), show the UI switching to fallback, highlight latency and cost delta on Console.
- Wrap: Walk through how rollback works and where logs/trace links live in the Console.

Communication templates (copyable):
- Incident brief to customer (short): "We detected elevated latency impacting X% of requests in region Y. We routed affected traffic to a validated compact variant to restore latency; expected impact: same intent accuracy, 15–25% lower token cost. ETA for full restoration: TBD (ops are provisioning capacity)."
- Post-incident summary: short bullets: cause, corrective actions, follow-ups, timeline, and a replay link.

Tradeoffs & guidance (one paragraph each):
- Quantized models: fastest recovery with minimal engineering work; may increase hallucination risk on sensitive tasks — validate on your eval prompts.
- Smaller architecture variants: lower cost and latency, but potential edge-case degradation; recommended for high-throughput background tasks.
- Caching: ideal for repeated prompts; cannot be used for user-specific dynamic content.
- Region failover: preserves availability but increases latency and may violate residency constraints if not pre-approved.

Operational checklist (pre-call prep):
- Confirm fallback variants have been smoke-tested on customer prompts (attach Confluence eval page).
- Ensure canary configs are present for demo models.
- Prepare the incident template and relevant tickets.

Next steps (owners & quick tasks):
- Priya Rao: Add 3 customer-specific eval sets to the fallback validation suite (JIRA-8142).
- Marcus Ng: Create a short Console walkthrough and two GIFs that show routing switch and cost delta (CONFLUENCE-5678).
- Diego Alvarez: Add an automated alert policy that triggers the fallback ladder at p95 > threshold (KPI alert).

Appendix: Helpful links and artifacts (for SEs)
- Confluence playbook: CONFLUENCE-5678
- Incident runbook: /incidents/fallbacks-runbook (internal link)
- Example API call for fallback routing: POST /v1/routing/change {"route":"/chat","model":"model-x-small-q8","duration":"15m"}

Notes to self (TODOs):
- We should A/B test user-perceived quality on quantized variants for top 5 pilot customers.
- Add a one-click Console action to toggle fallback for a single route.
